sentences.text: Italy has had 68 governments in 80 years. Who picks them?
Who can vote? Italian citizens from 18, at home or abroad.
You get two ballots, one per house. A cross on a party also counts for its local candidate.
Each area's winner takes a seat. The rest are shared out by party votes.
The Chamber of Deputies has 400 seats, the Senate 200, and every law must pass both.
In 2022, a centre-right alliance won both houses with 44% of the votes. The President named its leader, Giorgia Meloni, prime minister.
Both houses must back her. If that breaks, the President can name a new one, with no new vote. That's how Italy got to 68.
And the President? MPs and regional delegates elect him, for seven years. Sergio Mattarella signs every law.
Is it democracy if the prime minister can change without an election?
